headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write surfaces are documented, but docs-only evidence keeps uncertainty elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is docs-only and shows no I/O surfaces; agent B has clipboard, stdin/stdout, and filesystem inputs all false, plus no MCP. With no documented shared channel between ai-engineering-hub and pathway, a prompt-injection bridge is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, file handoff, or MCP bridge is added later, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing untrusted text as instructions by default, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not add an MCP server between them without provenance checks.
Review any future file-import path for instruction parsing.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile documents filesystem read/write, clipboard, screen capture, or network egress; agent B explicitly has network egress none and no file inputs, while agent A also has network egress none. With no shared workspace or data class overlap, leakage is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to shared sensitive files, leakage risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent starts uploading file contents to an external backend, reassess immediately.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave network egress disabled for both agents.
Confirm no hidden API upload path is enabled.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and agent A has no documented write or network surfaces. Because neither profile shows overlapping mutable-resource access, there is no credible capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF agent B gains write access to the same directory as agent A, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is given git write permissions, locking becomes relevant.
mitigations: Keep agent B read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
Do not grant git mutation rights to either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is weakly possible only if a future orchestrator treats ai-engineering-hub outputs as authoritative inputs to pathway. Today, agent B has no documented action-taking authority and no stdin/stdout or file inputs, so the pair lacks a default verification bypass; uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding A's outputs directly into B without validation, severity increases.
IF B is configured to execute downstream actions based on A-generated text, reassess.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B consumes A output.
Require schema validation on any A-to-B handoff.
Log and diff A outputs before downstream use.
requires-engineering: add provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are documented as touched by either agent, and both profiles are docs-only with no residency, retention, or regulated-data claims. Without a documented sensitive-data flow, there is no compliance mismatch to score for this pair.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent, compliance must be re-scored.
IF residency or retention policies are added to one agent but not the other, mismatch risk may appear.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and residency before deployment.
Review vendor terms if sensitive data is introduced.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated data.
